sentences.text: This animal was a small dinosaur measuring just over two meters in length.
Its body likely weighed around twenty-seven kilograms.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the creature to be two point two meters long and weigh twenty kilograms.
A larger species known as A. major grew between two point five and four meters and reached up to seventy pounds.
It possessed a large thumb claw and large eyes that sat forward on the skull rather than on the sides.
Several specimens are preserved as partially articulated skeletons despite being found in a high-energy river environment that usually scatters bones.
The initial discovery of this animal predates the description of any other dinosaur and is possibly the first known dinosaur from North America.
Sauropodomorph remains were first found in North America in 1818 in East Windsor, Connecticut, when Solomon Ellsworth Jr. uncovered bones nearly six feet long while digging a well.
When first discovered, the bones were initially mistaken for human remains until tail vertebrae proved otherwise.
The original type specimen of Anchisaurus polyzelus was discovered in 1855 by William Smith in Springfield, Massachusetts, while blasting a well for the Springfield Armory.
Fossils of Anchisaurus were first found in the Portland Formation of the Newark Supergroup in the Connecticut River Valley.
The first fossil of Anchisaurus was discovered in 1818 by Mr. Solomon Ellsworth while digging a well in East Windsor, Connecticut.
When first discovered, the bones were assumed to be human until they were reclassified as a dinosaur in 1855.
Evidence of gastroliths and a small sphenodont skull suggests Anchisaurus was omnivorous, eating mostly plants but occasionally meat.
The animal swallowed gastroliths to aid in digesting plant matter.
Its spoon-shaped teeth were adapted for ripping food.
The creature could turn its front legs inward to use them as grasping hands.
It had five toes on its feet that could be placed flat against the ground with strong ankles.
Anchisaurus had fewer, more widely spaced teeth and narrower feet compared to true prosauropods.
Anchisaurus is classified as a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur.
Recent studies show that Anchisaurus is closer to sauropods than to traditional prosauropods.
The genus Anchisaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1885.
The name Anchisaurus was coined as a replacement for Amphisaurus, which itself replaced Megadactylus, both of which had previously been used for other animals.
Recent research shows Anchisaurus is a true basal member of Sauropoda, with Prosauropoda forming a monophyletic sister group to Sauropoda.
The presence of tail bones led researchers to recognize the fossils as belonging to an indeterminate sauropodomorph, possibly closely related to prosauropods like Plateosaurus.
Anchisaurus lived during the Early Jurassic Period, approximately 200 to 192 million years ago, in what is now the Northeastern United States.
Anchisaurus lived in an arid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons between 200 and 195 million years ago.
Anchisaurus lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian stages, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
It is debated whether the Nova Scotia remains belong to Anchisaurus or represent a new taxon, Fendusaurus eldoni, though they suggest an omnivorous diet.
Some paleontologists debate whether Anchisaurus may have also eaten meat, given its position in the transition between herbivorous and carnivorous groups.
There is still some discussion regarding the diet of Anchisaurus.
